items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: I saw Jack, Count Basie's valet

ctx.x: ...it was over. It was over when he made records. But I was lucky in this way, Dan,, to work with Decca Records. This rarely happened. All because Cow Cow Davenport taught me the "Cow Cow Blues." I probably would have just been around, you know. But no, I had more initiative than just to be around, but I don't know if I would have ever had an opportunity to say that I played the Metropole or to say that I played the Apollo or to say that I played the Olympia in Paris, or that I played at the Salle Playel, or that…

play. This was in 1938 and they were stopping at the Woodside Hotel and I saw Jack, Count Basie's valet... he said that Mayo Williams was in town, looking for somebody to play for Cow Cow Davenport. I didn't say anything to him. I went and I met Mayo. We renewed our acquaintance. He/told me that if I ever come to New York, look him up.
